findings.evidence: `CoordinateRing` is `abbrev CoordinateRing : Type r := AdjoinRoot W'.polynomial` for `[CommRing R]` (mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point.lean:90, variable block line 80-82); `AdjoinRoot.mapRingEquiv` (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/AdjoinRoot.lean:417) and `WeierstrassCurve.map_baseChange` (mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Weierstrass.lean:285) are CommRing-only, as is `instance : IsScalarTower R R[X] W'.CoordinateRing` (Point.lean:104) used in the proof at line 77. The repo's own surrounding API is at that level: CoordinateRingMap.lean:99 `variable {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]`, docstring line 55 "Stated over arbitrary commutative rings; the curve need not be elliptic."
findings.fix: Split the variable block: state everything up to `coordinateRingGaloisAction_of` with `{R A : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (W : WeierstrassCurve R)` and `σ : A ≃ₐ[R] A`, then open a fields section for `functionFieldGaloisAction`.
findings.issue: `coordinateRingGaloisEquiv`, `coordinateRingGaloisAction` and their four lemmas (lines 55-153) never use `Field F`/`Field K`; they are stated one level above the object they act on. Only the `FunctionField` half (line 157 onward) needs fields.

findings.issue: `coordinateRingGaloisEquiv_algebraMap` (and hence `coordinateRingGaloisAction_algebraMap`, line 127) is the `p = C a` case of `coordinateRingGaloisEquiv_of`/`..._of` (lines 103, 147), but is proved separately with an 8-line calc instead of derived; the same `of (C b) = algebraMap` calc is then written a second time at lines 310-318.

findings.evidence: The proof only uses that the map fixes the generic coordinates and is semilinear on constants, and both hold for arbitrary `f`: `FunctionField.map` (FunctionField/Map.lean:101) with `map_genericX` (:131), `map_genericY` (:137), `map_algebraMap` (:115); the final step is `IsFractionRing.ringHom_ext`, which applies to ring homs into a different function field. Points transport by `Point.mapAlong` for an injective ring hom (Affine/Point/MapAlong.lean:84). Map.lean's own docstring (lines 40-46) already sets up this division of labour, putting the `W.map σ = W` identification in the Galois file and the general `f` in Map.lean.
findings.fix: State and prove the compatibility at the `FunctionField.map` level (e.g. a `Translation/Map.lean`) and obtain `functionFieldGaloisAction_translation` from it by the curve-equality transport, as `Isogeny/Frobenius/BaseChange.lean:78` already does with `▸`.
findings.issue: `functionFieldGaloisAction_translation` (with its two private generic-coordinate lemmas) proves translation compatibility only for `σ : K ≃ₐ[F] K`, although the identical computation proves it for the existing `FunctionField.map W f` along any `f : F →+* K`: `map W f (translation W P z) = translation (W.map f) (Point.mapAlong f f.injective P) (map W f z)`. The Galois case is then the `f = σ` instance plus the `(W⁄K).map σ = W⁄K` transport already used at line 55.

summary: The coordinate-ring half of the file carries unused `Field F`/`Field K` hypotheses although every object and lemma it touches is CommRing-level, the `algebraMap` lemmas are separately proved special cases of the `of` lemmas, and the translation-compatibility computation is confined to F-automorphisms when the same proof gives it for the existing `FunctionField.map` along any base homomorphism.
